brief.rationale: Conditions do not warrant standing down — the overnight move is only -0.3%, VIX at 15.3 remains in a low-vol regime, and index futures are down a fraction of a percent, so premium selling is still viable. However, three live risks argue for a step down from full config: an actively escalating US-Iran military conflict with unpredictable intraday headline risk, a hawkish repricing toward a September hike that leaves the market vulnerable to any Waller or Barr comment, and a soft-liquidity month-end session ahead of a heavy jobs week. I recommend delta_max 0.12 rather than the 0.15 config to push short strikes further from a potential headline-driven gap, and size_multiplier 0.55 to halve exposure while conditions clarify. No entries before 10:45 ET lets the opening gap fill or fail, absorbs the 10:30 Dallas Fed print, and avoids selling into the artificially wide open-print spreads typical of a geopolitical Monday. Reassess intraday if VIX breaks above 18 or if further strikes are reported, in which case size should drop again rather than the posture being loosened.

brief.rationale: Conditions do not meet the stand-down bar — there is no crash, no circuit breaker, and SPY is flat pre-open only ~2% off highs — but three independent tail risks are live simultaneously: an in-progress US-Iran military escalation, a fifth straight day of global bond selloff with yields at multi-year highs, and a Fed repricing toward a September hike rather than a cut. That combination raises the odds of a fast, headline-driven directional move that hurts 0-5 DTE short strikes far more than it hurts a delta-neutral book, so delta_max is tightened from 0.15 to 0.10 to buy meaningful strike buffer and size_multiplier is halved to 0.5 to cut per-trade loss on a gap. ADP at 08:15 lands pre-open and will be digested by the bell, but the opening range plus the 10:30 EIA petroleum print — which matters unusually much today because oil is the dominant macro driver — argue for holding entries until 11:00 rather than selling into unresolved morning vol. Note the 14:00 Beige Book as an intraday risk point for any position still open. Reassess and consider further de-risking ahead of Friday's NFP, which is the week's real event.

brief.rationale: Conditions are orderly, not extreme — a +0.17% gap, declining VXX, and sub-0.7% recent daily ranges — so a stand-down is not warranted and premium selling can proceed. However, today stacks an unusual number of catalysts: Waller speaking on inflation at 08:30 into a genuinely coin-flip rate-HIKE meeting, and ISM Services at 10:00 whose prices-paid component is the market's current obsession, which is why I gate entries until 10:15 to let the ISM reaction resolve rather than selling into the print. I cut delta_max to 0.10 from the 0.15 config because the active US-Iran conflict over the Strait of Hormuz is an untimed headline-gap risk that can jump through short strikes with no warning, and 0.15 deltas offer too little cushion for that tail. Size is halved to 0.5 primarily because tomorrow's NFP means anything beyond 0DTE carries an overnight event gap, compounded by AVGO earnings after today's close. The 5%+ Treasury yields and 30-year-high JGB yields are a slow-burn backdrop rather than an immediate trigger, but they argue against full sizing while the Fed path is unresolved.

brief.market_context: SPY closed 773.12 (+1.04%) Thursday near the top of a three-week 761-776 range, and is trading ~771.8 pre-market (-0.18%) after the 8:30 ET August payrolls print came in at 162k vs 53k consensus with unemployment steady at 4.1% — a 3x beat that sent short-end Treasury yields sharply higher and knocked futures off their highs. Vol is calm on the surface (VXX 17.65, down from 18.01; realized daily ranges under 1%), so this is a low-VIX tape rather than a stressed one. The unusual element is the policy direction: with Warsh as chair and Sept 16 FOMC hike odds near 50/50 pre-print, today's rates repricing is toward tightening, layered on an already-jittery long bond (10Y >5%, JGB yields at 30-year highs) and live US-Iran/Strait of Hormuz escalation with Brent in the low 90s.

brief.rationale: The single largest binary of the day, August payrolls, has already cleared before the open, which removes the classic reason to stand down and should let event IV bleed out of 0DTE — that argues for staying live rather than sitting out. However, a 3x consensus beat is exactly the kind of surprise that produces all-day directional trending as the market re-prices September FOMC hike odds, and post-NFP first-hour ranges are the most hostile environment for short-delta credit spreads, so I want no entries before 10:15 ET to let direction and IV settle. I am tightening delta_max to 0.12 from the 0.15 config because trend risk, not chop risk, is the dominant failure mode after a data surprise of this size, and wider strikes buy more room for a one-way drift. Size is cut to 0.6 for the combination of hawkish rates repricing, an unstable long bond, and live US-Iran headline risk that can hit intraday without warning. Conditions are elevated but entirely orderly — VXX is falling, SPY is near range highs, and there is no crash or liquidity event — so stand_down is not warranted.
